name: Account Creation
summary: Detailed breakdown of Phase 3 in the Taskly User Lifecycle — what happens from the moment a user taps 'Get Started' through completing email verification.

stages.name: Land on Sign-Up Screen
actions: Sees the sign-up form for the first time

emotions.label: Neutral
emotions.description: No strong reaction yet — the user is prepared for a form but hasn't been told what to expect.

painPoints: No indication of how long the sign-up process will take
No progress indicator to show how many steps are involved
opportunities: Show a 'Takes 30 seconds' reassurance below the heading
Add a subtle step progress bar at the top of the screen

stages.name: Enter Name
actions: Taps Next or moves to the email field
thoughts: Do they really need my full name?

emotions.label: Slightly annoyed
emotions.description: The full name requirement feels unnecessary for a to-do app — friction out of proportion to the ask.

painPoints: Field requires both first and last name with no explanation of why
No placeholder text showing the expected format
Keyboard doesn't auto-capitalise on Android devices
opportunities: Accept just a first name initially and ask for last name only when needed
Show a friendly placeholder like 'What should we call you?'

stages.name: Enter Email
actions: Moves on once the field shows as valid

emotions.label: Cautious
emotions.description: Privacy concern surfaces here — there's no explanation of what the email will be used for.

painPoints: No indication of what the email address is used for
Validation error fires on every keystroke, not just on blur
No privacy reassurance or link to privacy policy
opportunities: Add microcopy: 'We only use this to recover your account'
Validate on blur rather than on every keystroke
Add a small privacy reassurance note with a link to the privacy policy

stages.name: Create Password

emotions.label: Frustrated
emotions.description: Hidden requirements that only appear after failure create unnecessary friction and a sense of being tricked.

painPoints: Password requirements are not shown until after the first attempt fails
Strength indicator labels ('fair', 'good') are vague and don't guide the user
No show/hide toggle on the password field
opportunities: Show requirements upfront as a live checklist that ticks off as the user types
Replace vague strength labels with specific guidance ('Add a number or symbol')
Add a show/hide toggle to the password field

stages.name: Submit Form

emotions.label: Anxious
emotions.description: No feedback during submission creates uncertainty — the user can't tell if something is happening or if it's frozen.

painPoints: Button shows no loading state after being tapped
On failure, the error message is vague ('Something went wrong')
The password field is cleared on error, forcing the user to retype it
opportunities: Show a clear loading spinner on the button after tap
Display specific, actionable error messages ('That email is already registered — try signing in')
Preserve form state (especially the password field) on failure

stages.name: Email Verification
actions: Finds and opens the verification email
thoughts: Where's the email? Is it in spam?

emotions.label: Impatient
emotions.description: The wait for the verification email breaks momentum at the worst possible time — right after committing to sign up.

painPoints: Verification email takes 30–60 seconds to arrive
No resend option is available for the first 2 minutes
Tapping the verification link opens in the browser, not back in the app
opportunities: Reduce email delivery time to under 5 seconds via a dedicated transactional email service
Show an immediate 'Resend email' option with no delay
Use a deep link in the verification email to open directly in the app

insights.text: 6 of 8 usability test participants tapped an area where they expected a 'Continue with Google' button to be — it doesn't exist
Removing the 'last name required' validation and accepting just a first name increased form completion by 18% in a 2-week A/B test
5 of 8 usability test participants were confused about which password requirement they failed — requirements were only shown after a failed submission
3 of 8 usability participants abandoned the flow during the email verification wait — all three cited not knowing if it had worked as their reason
'Something went wrong' accounted for 100% of support tickets related to sign-up failures — users could not determine whether to retry or contact support

changelog.description: Journey data published with full research findings, pain points, opportunities, and insights
